title: God's 'sorrow' likewise puts the consequent for the antecedent
source_text: XIV. Eodem modo Deus propter hominum peccata contristari dicitur, non quod in se sentiat affectum aliquem nostrae tristitiae similem; sed simpliciter ad significandum hominum peccata Deo multum improbari atque displicere, & talia esse quae Deo tristitiam afferrent, si nostri similis esset, atque ὁμοιοπαθής: ita ut hic consequens pro antecedente sumatur, tristitia, scilicet, pro eo quod in subjecto capaci tristitiam gignere aptum est.
pass_a_gloss: In the same way God is said to be grieved on account of the sins of men, not that he feels in himself some affection like our sadness; but simply to signify that the sins of men are much disapproved by God and displease him, and are such as would bring sadness to God, if he were like us, and homoiopathes: so that here the consequent is taken for the antecedent, sadness, namely, for that which in a capable subject is apt to beget sadness.
pass_b_english: In the same way God is said to be grieved by human sins, not because he feels in himself any emotion like our sadness. It is simply a way of saying that God strongly disapproves of human sins and is displeased by them, and that they are such as would bring him sorrow if he were like us and subject to the same passions.
Here the consequent is put for the antecedent: sorrow stands for what is apt to produce sorrow in a subject capable of it.

lemmas.gloss: the consequent is taken for the antecedent

choices.why: The standard English term for God's knowing in advance; 'foreknowledge' is kept throughout for praescientia, with 'foresee' for praevidere.
